problem: Learning-based navigation planners need extensive task-specific training or fine-tuning and generalize poorly to novel scenes and objects, while prior VLM/ICL robotics work targets a single setup and often needs external perception modules.
motivation: Off-the-shelf VLMs carry common-sense reasoning that could transfer to navigation, but they need grounding in the deployment setup. Structured visual prompting plus a handful of retrieved in-context demonstrations could give that grounding without training or large data collection, and could work across sensing setups (onboard FPV camera or external CCTV TPV camera).
key_idea: Cast navigation as a VQA problem by overlaying numbered candidate actions or keypoints on the image, and condition a frozen VLM (Gemini 1.5 Pro) on MMR-retrieved annotated demonstrations injected as a fictitious multi-turn chat (history-injection ICL).
insight: A few demonstrations (about 1 episode per object, 25 in total) are enough for a frozen VLM to match or beat models trained on 8M episodes in novel scenes, while trained models win in known scenes. In TPV, the ICL context lifts TS from 147.82 (zero-shot) to 270.70 and cuts dangerous selections from 76 to 2. Context from other cameras, human trajectories, or web robot videos still helps (TS 219-247), so even non-target-domain context is useful. There is no ablation of MMR or the episodic memory.
method: Experiential Memory: a database of annotated images with chosen command and think-aloud explanation, collected from manual teleop, a human walking, other cameras, or web videos.
Sampler: retrieves context samples with Swin Transformer embeddings (mean of the last hidden layer), re-ranked with Maximal Marginal Relevance to balance similarity and diversity.

Annotator: overlays numbered action candidates. FPV uses a semicircle of 1-7 rotation/forward commands, with 8/9 for look up/down and 0 for DONE. TPV uses concentric circles of numbers around the YOLO-detected robot, filtered by a one-time SAM floor mask.

Episodic Memory (FPV only): a VLM-generated object list rendered as a rotating circular compass, plus last action, vertical view state and the previously planned commands. The VLM outputs the current and next action.

Prompt templating and history-injection ICL: k retrieved examples become fake query/answer chat turns, followed by the live annotated image. The output is JSON with the action sequence and explanation.

Controller: TPV uses a piecewise-linear path through the chosen points, tracked with a PD/PID controller (3-4 points replanned as they are tracked). FPV uses teleport-style discrete actions in AI2-THOR.

setting.backbone: Gemini 1.5 Pro (gemini-1.5-pro-001, frozen) + Swin Transformer retriever (+ YOLO, SAM in TPV)
setting.training_data: none (training-free); in-context memory of 25 manually teleoperated AI2-THOR episodes (FPV), and a handful of TurtleBot3/human/web-video trajectories (TPV)
setting.observation: monocular RGB (onboard FPV, or external fixed CCTV camera for TPV)
setting.action_space: FPV: discrete AI2-THOR actions (7 rotation/forward commands, look up/down, done). TPV: image-space keypoint sequences converted to waypoints for a PD controller
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (FPV); real-world rooms with a TurtleBot3 (TPV)
setting.privileged: none (TPV floor mask obtained once at setup via SAM; test objects differ from the memory objects)

numbers.eval_set_note: 300 episodes per scene type, max 25 steps; protocol of GVSN (Wang et al. 2024)

numbers_note: Zero-shot TPV baseline (TS 147.82, D 76) and ICL scenarios D (247.24, 8) and H (219.58, 13) also appear in Table tpv_res. The FPV table also has per-room results, not listed here. No standard benchmark splits are used.
results: In TPV, S2P raises the trajectory score from 147.82 (zero-shot) to 270.70 and cuts dangerous points from 76 to 2. In FPV AI2-THOR ObjectNav, it trails trained GVSN in known scenes (46.16 vs 83.73 SR), but in novel scenes and novel objects it reaches 38.95 SR / 28.62 SPL versus GVSN's 28.67 / 7.89. It uses only 25 demonstrations, against about 8M training episodes for GVSN.
limitations: Evaluation is small and non-standard: 300 episodes per scene type, a 25-step limit, and a custom TPV dataset with a self-defined TS metric. There are no ablations of MMR, the episodic memory, or the number of context samples.

The TPV floor mask is computed once and cannot handle new obstacles. The FPV controller teleports the agent, so control is not realistic. The approach depends on a closed VLM (Gemini) with latency and cost.
Weak in known scenes, and mixed across rooms (e.g. living room and bedroom SR are low in some splits).
